stackOverflowQuestions.title: Can anybody suggest another method to split a large Excel file into multiple files in any tool other than VBA?
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I need to split a large Excel file into multiple small files based on the first five digits of the values in a column. For example, I have values 1396A0001A,1396A0002A to split based on the first five digits, 1396A, into a separate sheet. I have VBA code to do this, but it is taking too much time - 3 hours to split the entire file of 15000 records in a file. Can you suggest any other method to split the file? Sub SplitSheetIntoMultipleWorkbooksBasedOnColumn() Dim objWorksheet As Excel.Worksheet Dim nLastRow As Integer, nRow As Integer, nNextRow As Integer Dim strColumnValue As String Dim objDictionary As Object Dim varColumnValues As Variant Dim varColumnValue As Variant Dim objExcelWorkbook As Excel.Workbook Dim objSheet As Excel.Worksheet Set objWorksheet = ActiveSheet nLastRow = objWorksheet.Range("A" & objWorksheet.Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row Set objDictionary = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary") For nRow = 2 To nLastRow strColumnValue = Left(objWorksheet.Range("F" & nRow).Value, 5) If objDictionary.Exists(strColumnValue) = False Then objDictionary.Add strColumnValue, 1 End If Next varColumnValues = objDictionary.Keys For i = LBound(varColumnValues) To UBound(varColumnValues) varColumnValue = varColumnValues(i) Set objExcelWorkbook = Excel.Application.Workbooks.Add Set objSheet = objExcelWorkbook.Sheets(1) objSheet.Name = objWorksheet.Name objWorksheet.Rows(1).EntireRow.Copy objSheet.Activate objSheet.Range("A1").Select objSheet.Paste objExcelWorkbook.SaveAs Filename:="C:\Users\User\Desktop\New folder\" & _ "01_03_" & varColumnValue & "_" & Format(Date, "yyyymmdd") & ".xlsx" For nRow = 2 To nLastRow If Left(CStr(objWorksheet.Range("F" & nRow).Value), 5) = CStr(varColumnValue) Then objWorksheet.Rows(nRow).EntireRow.Copy nNextRow = objSheet.Range("A" & objWorksheet.Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row + 1 objSheet.Range("A" & nNextRow).Select objSheet.Paste objSheet.Columns("A:H").AutoFit End If Next Next End Sub

stackOverflowQuestions.title: "Inbound Anomaly Score Exceeded" blocks legitimate multipart file uploads
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I've been trying to build a new tool for digtrace , the new tool take mp3 files that need to be uploaded by users. Site is behind Cloudflare (free plan). Basically is just a regular form, POST with multipart/form-data, MP3s up to 200MB plus a cover image. Nothing exotic. The uploads just die. No error on the page, nothing in my logs that made sense. From the server side it looked like empty POSTs arriving, so naturally I assumed my PHP was broken and spent way too long rewriting my form handling. That was a dead end. Turns out it was Cloudflare the whole time. Found it in the Security Events log: Managed Challenge on rule 949110, "Inbound Anomaly Score Exceeded", anomaly score 45. Normal home IPs, normal Chrome browsers, totally legit MP3 files. Cloudflare was throwing a challenge page at the upload request, and of course the file data doesn't survive that, so my server just saw a gutted request. No wonder my code "looked broken". The really annoying part is what 949110 actually is. It's not one rule catching something specific, it's the OWASP totalizer, it adds up a bunch of small paranoia-level hits and fires when the total crosses the line. Binary file data in a multipart body trips enough of those little rules that a perfectly innocent MP3 pushes it over. There's no single thing to fix in the file, the file is fine. And it doesn't happen from every connection, which is exactly why it took me so long. I'd test an upload from my end and get a clean 200 back, then a user on a different network gets challenged. If your uploads fail for some people but not others, go check Security Events before you touch your code. Seriously. Now here's where I'm stuck. quantaArticles.description: Comb jellies are helping answer fundamental questions in biology, from how the earliest nervous systems evolved to how bioluminescence works.
quantaArticles.author: Marlowe Starling

quantaArticles.title: Black Holes or Black Hole Stars? Astronomers Spar Over Webb Telescope’s ‘Little Red Dots.’
quantaArticles.description: The James Webb Space Telescope spots mysterious “little red dots” everywhere. A bold new theory suggests they’re suns dozens of times larger than our entire solar system.
quantaArticles.author: Charlie Wood

quantaArticles.title: Why Do These Fossil Shells Flip Their Spirals Every Few Millennia?
quantaArticles.description: The mystery of the flipping foraminifera may conceal a rarely observed evolutionary process playing out across the planet.
quantaArticles.author: Fanni Daniella Szakál

infoqArticles.title: Alibaba Open Sources OpenCodeReview for AI-Assisted Code Review
infoqArticles.description: Alibaba recently open-sourced OpenCodeReview, an AI-powered code review CLI that combines deterministic pipelines for file selection, bundling, and rule matching with an LLM agent for dynamic code analysis. It supports built-in checks for issues such as null-pointer exceptions, thread safety, XSS, and SQL injection. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Google Agent Development Kit for Kotlin Reaches Feature Parity with Python, Supports On-Device AI
infoqArticles.description: Google has released the Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Kotlin 1.0, a production-ready framework for building AI agents across Kotlin, Android, and JVM/server applications. It brings Kotlin to feature parity with Google's ADK for Python and Java, while adding Android-specific capabilities for on-device and hybrid AI. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Measures Origin TLS Preferences, Cutting Handshake Retries from 52% to 3.7%
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has replaced its static X25519 guess for origin TLS handshakes with per-origin measurement. HelloRetryRequests on scanned origins fell from roughly 52% to 3.7%, removing over 150 ms from p90 latency. Post-quantum connections completing in one round trip rose from 0% to 99.2%, though only 12.8% of origins support it. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Context Engineering at LinkedIn: How We Built an Organizational Context Layer for AI Agents with MCP
infoqArticles.description: Ajay Prakash discusses how LinkedIn overcomes AI agent limitations in large codebases. He explains Contextual Agent Playbooks and Tools - built on Model Context Protocol (MCP) - which serves procedural memory, code search, and runbooks directly to coding agents. Prakash shares architectural details and operational guardrails that deliver a 20% productivity boost with zero loss in reliability. By A
infoqArticles.author: Ajay Prakash

infoqArticles.title: AWS Lambda Pushes Serverless Toward Long-Running Workloads
infoqArticles.description: AWS Lambda now allows functions running on Lambda Managed Instances to run for up to 90 minutes, six times longer than the previous 15-minute limit, further blurring the line between a Lambda invocation and a traditional server. The limit remains unchanged for traditional synchronous requests. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: SolidStart 2: Replaces Vinxi with a Vite 8 and Enters Maintenance as Its Role Winds Down
infoqArticles.description: SolidStart, a full-stack meta-framework based on SolidJS, has transitioned to version 2.0, improving compatibility with Vite's Environment API. This release modernizes the framework, enhancing CSS handling and integrating better with tools like Tailwind CSS and deployment services. Following this, SolidStart has been placed in maintenance mode as its capabilities are incorporated into Solid 2.0. B
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: MariaDB 13 Expands Oracle Compatibility and Improves Developer Experience and Observability
infoqArticles.description: MariaDB Community Server 13.0 has reached General Availability (GA) and is now officially stable. This release introduces a range of new features, deprecations, and performance improvements, including expanded support for procedural SQL, new DML capabilities, and more. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: DoorDash Uses Multi Agent LLMs to Clean up 60,000 Feature Flags
infoqArticles.description: DoorDash built a multi-agent LLM system to automate stale feature flag cleanup across more than 60,000 flags and 623 repositories. The workflow combines live experimentation data through MCP, engineer approval, isolated Git worktrees, parallel agents, and automated validation. In an evaluation of 50 flags, 45 produced usable pull requests at an average of 13.8 minutes and $4.79 per cleanup. By Lee
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: WSO2 Releases Agent Manager as Enterprises Look to Control Growing AI Agent Sprawl
infoqArticles.description: WSO2 has announced the general availability of WSO2 Agent Manager, an open-source platform designed to provide centralized governance, identity management, security controls, and operational oversight for AI agents running across different models, frameworks, and deployment environments. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Complexity and Creativity in Software Engineering
infoqArticles.description: Phillip Mortimer discusses the shift toward write-only software driven by AI code generation. He explains why traditional pull requests are broken and shares how engineering leaders can manage complexity by decoupling intent from implementation, automating code reviews, and building self-healing architecture to unleash developer creativity across senior engineering and architecture teams. By Phill
infoqArticles.author: Phillip Mortimer

infoqArticles.title: htmx 4.0: a Fetch-Based Rewrite, Built-In Morphing Swaps, and Explicit Attribute Inheritance
infoqArticles.description: htmx 4 has been released, featuring a transition from XMLHttpRequest to the fetch() API, enhancing streaming capabilities. Key updates include built-in morphing swaps for DOM state preservation and an hx-partial tag for cleaner updates. Attribute inheritance is now explicit, with event names standardized. The library maintains focus on minimal JavaScript while remaining popular among frameworks. B
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Podcast: Signals and Levers: Building Thriving Engineering Organizations
infoqArticles.description: In this podcast Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods spoke to Elisabeth Hendrickson and Joel Tosi about systems thinking as a lens for software delivery, the cultural "levers" leaders and teams can pull to shape organizations, and building thriving, sustainable teams amid AI-driven change. By Elisabeth Hendrickson, Joel Tosi
infoqArticles.author: Elisabeth Hendrickson, Joel Tosi

infoqArticles.title: Article: Architecting Secure and Scalable Facial Verification Systems
infoqArticles.description: When three thousand employees verify at once, synchronous API calls collapse. This article presents a four-layer architecture for high-volume face verification: client-side filtering that cut cloud costs 30%, decoupled detection and verification enabling 10x scaling, risk-based dynamic thresholds, and zero-trust privacy with consent gates and automated data purging for GDPR and HIPAA. By Praveen K
infoqArticles.author: Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan

infoqArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces Triage Framework and Case Studies to Report Model Misalignment
infoqArticles.description: OpenAI has released a disclosure framework for model misalignment during its lifecycle. Employees can flag potential issues, prompting technical staff to label incidents. The initial case studies outline unexpected model behaviours, providing insights into deviations from expected parameters. Community reactions show both approval and scepticism regarding transparency and corporate narratives. By
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Building an Internal Developer Platform with Artificial Intelligence
infoqArticles.description: Agents are becoming the new developer platform, using semantic search with data from tools like Git, Slack, and Jira for context. Things to consider are setting guardrails to block or allow things, and using logs, metrics, and traces to understand agent behavior. By Ben Linders
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders
